meta_description: Zero-trust across 214 schools — student-data privacy audit closed and ransomware-ready segmentation without touching classroom uptime

blocks.x: Zero-trust across 214 schools, student-data privacy audit closed and ransomware-ready segmentation without touching classroom uptime

Identity withheld, a school district whose network was flat, whose student data was everywhere, and whose ransomware peer districts were a growing list. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline assessment mapped the exposure: student-data systems reachable from every classroom device, 3,100 staff accounts with legacy access, and a privacy-audit finding list the district had carried two cycles.
The constraint was instructional: nothing could interrupt classroom technology during school hours, and the previous provider's attempt had gone home to 900 angry emails.

We ran the program at classroom speed: segmentation waves executed after hours with fallback drills as part of each wave, student-data systems isolated behind identity-first access, staff access right-sized with leaver automation, and the privacy findings tracked to evidence the auditors walked. Classroom uptime was never touched; the audit list was.
